findings.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
findings.trigger: If an attacker inputs a format string with additional format specifiers or escape sequences.
findings.assumptions: The code does not explicitly execute any OS commands, but if an attacker can control the format string, it could lead to unexpected behavior or information exposure.

findings.title: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
findings.trigger: If the input value exceeds the range of int64_t, it could lead to integer overflow.
findings.assumptions: The code does not check if the input value fits within the int64_t range.

findings.title: OS Command Injection
findings.trigger: If an attacker inputs a value that includes special characters or escape sequences.
findings.assumptions: The code does not execute any OS commands, but if an attacker can control the input, it could lead to unexpected behavior or information exposure.

findings.title: Improper Input Validation
findings.trigger: If the input value does not meet expected criteria (e.g., non-numeric input).
findings.assumptions: The code does not validate the input to ensure it is a valid int64_t value.
